subject: Production latency spike: p95/p99 regressions + tokens/sec drop (Glacier Retail)
messages:
From: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@glacierretail.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 latency + tokens/sec drop — production impact

Jordan —

We started seeing a significant jump in p95 and p99 latency on our production hosted endpoints around 04:30 PT this morning. Concurrently, our tokens/sec throughput on the endpoint has dropped roughly 40% compared to the baseline last week. The degradation looks intermittent but is causing timeouts in our real-time personalization pipeline.

What we see in our metrics (attached):
- p95 latency increased from ~220ms to ~1.2s
- p99 latency spiked to ~2.6s for a subset of requests
- tokens/sec dropped from ~2,200 to ~1,300 for median payloads
- error rate increased from 0.2% to ~1.8% (mostly 504 timeouts)

We believe the change lines up with an update your team pushed early this morning — can you confirm? We need an ETA on a mitigation. This is impacting a critical morning batch run.

Attaching: p95_p99_dashboard.png (screenshot), brief logs.

Thanks,
Sam Lewis
Head of Platform Engineering
Glacier Retail

Folks — quick summary of initial findings from runtime side:
- There was a canary rollout of a kernel selector tweak and an updated quantized execution path at 04:12 PT. Canary ran across 10% of capacity and then was promoted to 100% at ~04:30 PT after automated checks.
- Our early telemetry shows a clear correlation between the promotion and the tokens/sec regression for requests with sequence lengths > 512. The quantized kernel path increases memory stalls on some instances leading to lower tokens/sec and higher p95/p99.
- Error rate uptick is likely from transient queueing and timeouts due to the slower token production.

Attachments: kernel_rollout_diff.patch (diff of selector), kernel_metrics_snapshot.csv (snapshot taken at 09:30).

Immediate recommendation: revert kernel selector to previous policy for hosted endpoints that serve Glacier Retail and a handful of other sensitive accounts, and re-run load tests. If Jordan approves, I can run the rollback now (takes ~8 minutes to fully converge).

Technical note (brief): the change attempted to push quantized matrix mul variants for certain attention dims; the fast-path assumption doesn't hold for our small-batch, long-seq workload. We'll instrument a targeted fallback for sequences > 512.

-David
David Kim

Redwood Inference

Our engineering and reliability teams are observing the cluster now and see p95/p99 returning toward baseline; tokens/sec is trending back up (preliminary numbers show ~90% of baseline restored).

- Rolled back selector promotion for hosted runtime (converged by ~10:26 PT)
- Pinned Glacier endpoints to previous kernel variant to prevent re-promotion
- Opened incident INF-2342 and collected metrics/trace data for RCA
